summary.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR2,995 crore and PAT 22% to INR103 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR222 crore on cost inflation and El Niño.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 17% YoY to INR2,995 crore, with EBITDA stable at INR222 crore (7.4% margin), PBT up 5% to INR131 crore and PAT up 22% to INR103 crore. H1 revenue rose 13% to INR5,847 crore, while H1 EBITDA and PBT declined modestly and H1 PAT was INR231 crore. El Niño, a 40%-odd June rain deficit and dairy milk-price inflation hit crop care, Astec and dairy margins, while animal nutrition, oil palm and B2C foods carried the quarter. Management said it is still chasing double-digit PBT growth for FY27 but described the environment as tougher than the prior call.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA and PBT declined modestly YoY

financial_highlights.value: 21 days (management cited 22 days on the Q&A call)
financial_highlights.change: From 32 days last year (Q&A cited 31 days)
Q&A cited B2C salience moving from 25% to 35%
Debt up roughly INR200-300 crore vs March per analyst

financial_highlights.value: About INR50 crore received this quarter
financial_highlights.change: No one-offs in other income per CFO

segments.name: Animal nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue +14% and segment profit +32% YoY on realisations and volumes; volume +3% as broiler feed was deliberately de-prioritised, while cattle feed grew ~8% and layer feed double digits. Shrimp feed business exited.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28% and segment profit +4%; FFB volumes +14% in Q2. OER fell to ~18.9% in Q2 (vs 18.8% in Q1) due to heat stress. Added 13,000 ha in H1; Khammam integrated complex inaugurated with mill, CPKO refinery and biogas plant commissioned.

segments.name: Crop care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew on a low base but profitability fell on El Niño-led demand weakness and adverse product mix. Ashitaka maize herbicide expected to cross INR100 crore first-year revenue.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Weak enterprise demand and lower realisations offset CDMO growth; EBITDA hit by elevated input costs. Management flagged weak US and Brazil markets.

segments.name: Dairy
segments.commentary: Revenue +6% on calibrated pricing; profitability hit by elevated milk procurement, packaging and logistics costs. Management expects no milk-price respite for about two quarters.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: B2C grew 50% with salience at 38%. EBITDA plus working media margin 5.8% vs 5.6% last year. About 25% of current business from products launched in the last year.

segments.name: ACI Godrej (Bangladesh JV)
segments.commentary: Delivered strong volume, revenue and profit growth; management said volumes grew at high double digits across aqua, poultry and dairy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PBT double-digit growth is still being chased but management said it is tougher and more clarity will come monthly; not a firm commitment.
Oil palm: OER expected to recover toward ~19.7% for the year; aim to end FY at last year's annualised OER level.
Oil palm FFB volume growth guided at double digits for FY27 and FY28; cyclone assessment shows no tree damage.
Oil palm mid-term (2-4 years): downstream PKO derivatives expected to add ~2 percentage points to oil palm EBITDA margin; meaningful impact from Q4 FY27 and scaling in FY28.
Oil palm EBITDA: management aims for a healthy double-digit CAGR over FY27 and the mid-term (FY26 oil palm EBITDA about INR426 crore).
Astec CDMO mid-term share targeted at 50-55% of business; FY27 expected to be a tough year.
capex_capacity: Khammam integrated oil palm complex inaugurated: mill, CPKO refinery and biogas plant commissioned in Q2 (PKO derivatives plant operational from 1 September); full hydrogenation and fractionation in December, second scale-up phase in December.
Plantations: 13,000 ha added in H1 FY27.
Agchem pipeline: three new products to launch this year (including soybean herbicide Ghassnash launched this month), 1-2 new launches a year, targeting seven crop segments by FY29-30.
Astec CDMO: about 90% of Q2 inquiries converted to R&D; around 15 products in R&D pipeline; management expects 70-80% R&D-to-commercialisation conversion.
Sales transformation CoE hired head from Britannia and Marico; two more members to join by December.
demand_pricing: Monsoon ended about 13% below normal; June rainfall about 40% deficit; reservoirs at 10-year low, raising Rabi risk for agchem.
Oil palm: September OER back to last year's level and October marginally ahead; Q2 FFB collections at an all-time high.

Palm oil: management expects CPO to range INR4,250-4,400 over the next couple of months, creeping up from February-March; Brent volatility and Malaysian inventory cited. PKO volatility lower than CPO.
Andhra Pradesh fruit price order for the new year not yet issued; last year's order assumed 20.01% OER; management hopes for a lower rate but cannot guide.
Dairy: no respite in milk prices for about two quarters (El Niño cattle productivity hit) plus structural value-added shift.
Broiler feed deliberately de-prioritised; management said it could have added thousands of tonnes given inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Oil palm plantation health in Andhra Pradesh after the drought and cyclones; is 10%+ FFB growth still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cyclones refilled soil water with no widespread tree damage; Q2 FFB grew double digits despite three extreme-heat months, and FY27 double-digit FFB growth stands.

qa_highlights.question: Contribution from the PKO derivatives plant and margin impact in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant opened 1 September, so no meaningful Q2 contribution; meaningful impact from Q4 and scale-up in FY28, adding ~2 percentage points to oil palm EBITDA margin over 2-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for palm oil prices and Andhra Pradesh OER pricing order?
qa_highlights.answer: CPO expected in INR4,250-4,400 range near term, rising from February-March if El Niño persists; AP order not yet out and management cannot guide on the outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Dairy pricing environment and any relief?
qa_highlights.answer: No relief for about two quarters: temporary El Niño-driven productivity loss plus a structural shift to value-added products that resets milk pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Update on FY27 PBT guidance and debt increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Double-digit PBT still chased but harder. Debt rose on deliberate inventory build ahead of inflation; working capital days cut to about 22 (cited); debt-to-equity about 0.8 and expected to stay around that level in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Poultry margin trajectory and dairy GTM revamp?
qa_highlights.answer: Dairy GTM simplification with an AM/PM distributor pilot in Chennai, with ~18 months of correction. Foods margins under pressure as B2C shift; EBITDA plus working media margin up 20bps to 5.8%.

risks_watch: El Niño impact on Rabi season and agchem demand (cotton, chilli); management expects a couple of years of structural correction in crop care and Astec.
Oil palm OER recovery from ~18.9% in Q2 toward 19.7%+ and the upcoming Andhra Pradesh fruit price order.
Palm and PKO price volatility tied to crude, biodiesel mandates and Malaysian inventories.
Dairy milk procurement costs with no price relief for about two quarters; heavy inflation across feed inputs.
Rising debt and inventory build; H2 cash release needed to hold debt-to-equity near 0.8.
Rising employee costs from sales transformation hires, annualising into FY28.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the outlook: management said agchem is facing a structural correction and FY27 PBT growth is harder, while staying confident on oil palm volumes and the B2C foods shift. Tone was most defensive on dairy pricing and the PBT target, and most upbeat on oil palm and ACI Godrej.
key_quotes: Let me tell you from last time, the environment's a little tougher. I'll be very honest, like always, it's a bit of an understatement.
We are pretty confident that I mean, our attempt is very clearly, can we recover over the next four months and end the year at that 19.7 plus kind of a number?
The answer is no. We are not seeing any respite.
I will give you CAGR. I think a healthy double-digit CAGR is what we chase, and we think we should be able to deliver over this year itself, and over the midterm also.
